name: Citizenship by Investment Programme (CIP)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a non-refundable contribution of at least US$230,000 to the National Development Fund, for a family of up to 4.
Principal applicant must be at least 18 years old.
Requires passing due diligence checks (police certificate, medical certificate, source-of-funds review).
Requires purchase of approved real estate worth at least US$300,000, held for a minimum of 5 years.
Principal applicant must be at least 18 years old.
Requires passing due diligence checks (police certificate, medical certificate, source-of-funds review).
Requires investment of at least US$1,500,000 in an approved business as a single investor, or a joint investment totalling at least US$5,000,000 with a minimum of US$400,000 per investor.
Principal applicant must be at least 18 years old.
Requires passing due diligence checks (police certificate, medical certificate, source-of-funds review).

requirement_groups.name: University of the West Indies (UWI) Fund contribution

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a non-refundable contribution of at least US$260,000 (inclusive of processing fees) to the UWI Fund, for a family of up to 5, including at least one scholarship place at the UWI Five Islands Campus.
Principal applicant must be at least 18 years old.
Requires passing due diligence checks (police certificate, medical certificate, source-of-funds review).

evidence_required.document: Government processing fee: US$10,000 (single applicant) or US$20,000 (family up to 4, plus US$10,000 per additional dependant), 10% payable non-refundable on submission
Due diligence fees: US$8,500 (principal), US$5,000 (spouse), US$2,000 (dependant 12-17), US$4,000 (dependant 18+), US$0 (dependant 0-11)
Passport issuance fee: US$300 per applicant

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: at least 5 days' physical presence in Antigua and Barbuda within the first 5 calendar years after obtaining citizenship (real estate investors must also hold the property for a minimum of 5 years); failure results in citizenship revocation and forfeiture of the investment

sources.title: Citizenship by Investment Unit, Government of Antigua and Barbuda -- Schedule of Fees: NDF ($230,000), real estate ($300,000), business investment ($1,500,000 single / $5,000,000 joint at $400,000+ per person), UWI Fund ($260,000), government processing fees, due diligence fees by family member, passport fee

Citizenship by Investment Unit, Government of Antigua and Barbuda -- Citizenship page: 5-day physical presence requirement within 5 calendar years of obtaining citizenship, 5-year real-estate holding period, revocation and forfeiture on non-compliance
Wikipedia -- Antiguan and Barbudan nationality law: minimum age 18 for principal CIP applicants

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Antigua and Barbuda's initial build -- the flagship Citizenship by Investment Programme (CIP), administered by the CIU under the Citizenship by Investment Act. All four investment pathways are folded into one file as OR-groups since they share the same due diligence process, fee structure, and outcome (immediate citizenship, no residence requirement before naturalisation). IMPORTANT LIVE-POLICY FLAG: as of this pass, the current, tier-1-confirmed physical-presence obligation is 5 days within 5 years post-citizenship. Multiple tier-3/4 sources report a Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Bill 2026 was presented to Parliament on 14 July 2026 that would raise this to 30 days within 5 years, with Prime Minister Gaston Browne reportedly stating a 30-day standard 'has already been applied administratively' under an Eastern Caribbean regional framework -- this administrative-practice claim was NOT independently confirmed via cip.gov.ag directly in this pass, so the route is modelled on the last tier-1-confirmed figure (5 days) rather than the reported-but-unconfirmed 30-day practice; re-verify against cip.gov.ag once the amendment's status is confirmed. Investment amounts are stated in the source without a currency symbol on the fee schedule page but are consistently described in US dollars across CIP marketing/legal materials generally -- modelled as USD.
